T1.pages: Transformer PDF p.4, section 3.2.1 and footnote 4
T1.expected: softmax(QK^T/sqrt(d_k))V; large dot products saturate softmax and yield tiny gradients; unit-variance independent components give dot-product variance d_k.

T3.expected: Mask future decoder self-attention logits to minus infinity before softmax; shifted target embeddings preserve autoregression. A current-position mask entry is allowed for shifted representations.

T5.expected: 28.4 BLEU on WMT14 EN-DE; 3.5 days on eight P100 GPUs.

T6.pages: Transformer PDF p.9, Table 3(A) and accompanying text
T6.expected: At constant compute: 1,4,8,16,32 heads give 24.9,25.5,25.8,25.8,25.4 development BLEU. Single head is 0.9 below best; more heads is not monotonically better.

M1.expected: Helium is the text autoregressive Transformer backbone. Mimi is the streaming neural audio codec combining semantic/acoustic information, RVQ and distillation. Multi-stream joint modeling is performed by the streaming Depth/Temporal Transformer design, not by the codec alone.

M3.expected: Inner Monologue adds time-aligned text as a per-frame prefix before semantic/acoustic tokens, providing linguistic scaffolding and improved speech quality. Relative text/audio delay derives ASR/TTS. Separate speaker streams are the multi-stream mechanism. PDF p.28 is audio-LM benchmarking and does not establish the ASR/TTS delay mechanism.

M4.expected: 160 ms theoretical and about 200 ms practical. Mimi at 12.5 Hz contributes an 80 ms frame; one additional semantic-to-acoustic delay frame yields 160 ms. Causal streaming codec, efficient RQ hierarchy and multi-stream speech avoid a cascaded turn-based pipeline. Acoustic delay is distinct from relative text/audio delay used for ASR/TTS. Inner Monologue marginally increases inference work (17 instead of 16 generated tokens), rather than reducing cross-modal decoding work. The PDF does not promise 200 ms on a typical CPU.

M6.expected: Audio leads/text delayed -> ASR, teacher-force audio and sample text. Text leads/audio delayed -> TTS, teacher-force text and sample audio. The experimental delay is two seconds; no architecture/loss/data changes are needed between the task configurations.

H1.expected: Fixed-vocabulary handcrafted BPE segmentation is not learned jointly; tokenization has character/language/modality limitations. A fully learned tokenization-LM-detokenization hierarchy may scale better. Appendix H's tokenization-bias discussion concerns impossible exact online reconstruction of BPE boundaries with future-byte information; it does not establish all asserted downstream causal consequences or a requirement to learn detokenization.

H2.pages: H-Net PDF p.6, equation 4, section 2.2.1; contrast cited pp.2,17
H2.expected: Use learned query/key projections of adjacent encoder outputs; p_t=(1-cos(q_t,k_{t-1}))/2, b_t=1[p_t>=0.5], p_1=1. Low similarity implies high boundary probability. Keep boundary-marked vectors. Cited pp.2,17 mention similarity routing but omit the inverse mapping, threshold and selection details.

H4.expected: Encoder preserves fine-grained residuals and builds representations for chunking; main network concentrates capacity on the compressed sequence; decoder combines dechunked coarse output with encoder residuals at original resolution. Outer Mamba-2 networks suit long fine-grained inputs and compression; main network may be a Transformer or recursive H-Net. No lossless guarantee.

H6.pages: H-Net PDF pp.12-13, Figure 3 and Table 2
H6.expected: Two-stage is stronger than one-stage at the compared Large/XL scales. XL crossover bytes: two-stage 30B, one-stage 100B, space 200B; all three eventually cross. Table 2 two-stage minus one-stage mean zero-shot accuracy is 55.5-53.6=1.9 points (Large), 58.2-56.2=2.0 (XL). The 2.2/2.6-point statement on p.12 is versus Transformer, not one-stage.

X1.pages: Transformer PDF pp.3,5,7; H-Net PDF pp.4-6
X1.expected: Transformer uses externally preprocessed BPE/word-piece tokens with variable sequence lengths and variable-length subword pieces. H-Net learns content/context-dependent chunk boundaries over raw inputs end-to-end, with chunk/dechunk hierarchy. The configured stage count is fixed for a model, not dynamically varying hierarchy depth per example. Cite both papers.
